question: when is it ok to use @here or @channel in slack?
answer: Only for urgent or time-sensitive posts that need everyone in the channel's immediate attention, e.g. a last-minute meeting link change or urgent outage help.
evidence: p52: @channel or @here mentions should be reserved for urgent or time-sensitive posts that require immediate attention

question: how big a week-to-week jump in my product's total infra spend should set off an alert?
answer: Alert when total product cost changes by more than 15% week over week. For individual components the threshold is more than 25%.
evidence: p996: Total product cost: alert if week-over-week change > 15%

question: as an engineer can i be on two product teams at the same time?
answer: No. Product engineers should never be in more than one team because it undermines ownership. Only supporting roles like PMs and designers can span teams.
evidence: p152: product engineers should never be in more than one team because this acts against proper ownership.

question: what size should the main image at the top of a blog post be?
answer: 1200x630 pixels, the Open Graph size. That's roughly double display size, so it looks crisp on HiDPI screens.
evidence: p825: Open Graph images are 1200x630, so we stick with those dimensions to keep this simple.

question: if a marketing candidate writes something during their superday, do we publish it?
answer: No. The SuperDay task is usually real marketing work, like creating content or talking to customers, but the work isn't actually published.
evidence: p934: creating a piece of content or talking to customers, though we don't actually publish the work

question: what's the default spending cap on posthog ai for customers?
answer: $150 by default. The data warehouse's default limit is $500.
evidence: p864: The default limit for the data warehouse is $500, and $150 for PostHog AI

question: how much can i spend each quarter on trips to hang out and work with teammates in person?
answer: Everyone has a $1,500 quarterly travel budget for ad-hoc meetups.
evidence: p59: Everyone also has a $1,500 quarterly travel budget for ad-hoc meetups.

question: should i put the link directly in my linkedin post?
answer: No. The algorithm penalises direct links. Say "link in comments" and add it about 6 hours later, or include an image.
evidence: p162: The algorithm hates direct posts to links.

question: what's the end goal of posthog's secret master plan?
answer: Ship every tool and all the data engineering teams need, use it to speed up the ship-observe-iterate cycle, then eventually automate that entire cycle.
evidence: p1071: Eventually, automate the entire cycle

question: do regular session recordings get saved in postgres?
answer: No. Only pinned or persisted (LTS) recordings are written to PostgreSQL. Regular recordings live in ClickHouse's session_replay_events table, with the data in S3.
evidence: p406: Regular session recordings (not pinned/persisted) do NOT write to PostgreSQL - they only exist in ClickHouse session_replay_events table

question: how many people usually get put on a brand new product at the start?
answer: Just 1 or 2 people. We don't spin up a whole team on day one.
evidence: p908: New products start with just 1 or 2 people - we don't spin up a whole team on day 1.

question: a reviewer left a comment on my pr with no tag in front of it, do i have to fix it before i merge?
answer: No. A comment without a prefix counts as a suggestion, so it's your call. Only 'blocking:' comments must be fixed before merge.
evidence: p322: If a comment doesn't have a prefix, assume it's a suggestion.

question: just started as a pm, how many customer calls should i set up in my first week?
answer: Arrange and host at least 2 customer calls, set up through customer success at first, to get feedback on ongoing projects.
evidence: p963: Arrange and host 2+ calls (through customer success initially) and get feedback from customers about ongoing projects

question: what time of day should i run the monthly product update call for the sales and CS folks?
answer: Ideally 8–10 AM Pacific, so as many people as possible can join live. Make sure it is recorded.
evidence: p644: 8-10 AM Pacific time is an ideal slot here

question: why are there engineers working in marketing?
answer: We hire full-stack developers into marketing so tutorials, docs and posts can cover the full technical depth they need.
evidence: p805: We even hire full-stack developers into our marketing team to make sure we can cover the full depth

question: a yc startup reached out trying to sell us their product, should we actually buy it?
answer: Take them seriously and buy it if it's genuinely valuable and safe to do so. Otherwise, give them direct feedback.
evidence: p1035: if a YC company reaches out, take them seriously and buy their product

question: how much do we pay eng candidates for the superday?
answer: $1,000 USD for the paid full day of work.
evidence: p922: The SuperDay is a paid full day of work ($1,000 USD).

question: i'm putting up a popup inside the product to announce a feature, do i need to do anything with the feature flag behind it?
answer: Yes. Add the Marketing tag to the feature flag that powers the prompt, so others can track which in-app messages are being shown.
evidence: p11: Add the Marketing tag to the feature flag used to power your in-app prompt

question: i'm an engineer, how long should i try to figure something out myself before asking someone for help?
answer: Try on your own for at least 1 hour, but don't stay totally stuck for more than 2 hours before asking for help.
evidence: p801: for at least 1 hour, but don't remain totally stuck on something for more than 2 hours

question: how many accounts can an account manager have before we stop sending them new leads?
answer: Once a TAM reaches 15 managed customers or $1.5m ARR, stop generating new product-led leads for them, and flag it to Simon.
evidence: p685: Once a TAM has hit 15 managed customers or ARR of $1.5m, we should stop generating new product-led leads

question: how many paying customers does a new product need before we say it's found its fit?
answer: Five delighted, paying customers. That's the bar for product-market fit within PostHog's platform.
evidence: p810: working with customers until we have five delighted, paying customers.

question: i just got handed a brand new account. which approach to growing it should i start with in the first few months?
answer: Go deeper: help the existing team adopt more products. For a new account's first 90 days, the handbook says always start there.
evidence: p582: New account, first 90 days | Go deeper (always start here)

question: is there parking at hogpatch if i drive in?
answer: Yes. The building's garage fits 4–5 cars and is for employees only. Ask for a fob, or tell Judy beforehand for a one-off visit.
evidence: p942: We have a garage in the building that allows up to 4–5 cars max.

question: how do i stop vitally from sending the automated second onboarding email to a customer i'm already chatting with?
answer: Switch the account to the Onboarding Completed status. That blocks the second outreach, though the graduation email will still send.
evidence: p895: To stop the automation, you can flip the account to the Onboarding Completed status.
